title.value: TANGO: a placebo-controlled randomized phase 2 study of efficacy and safety of the anti-tau monoclonal antibody gosuranemab in early Alzheimer’s disease
title.quote: TANGO: a placebo-controlled randomized phase 2 study of efficacy and safety of the anti-tau monoclonal antibody gosuranemab in early Alzheimer’s disease

design.value: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multiple-dose phase 2 trial with a 78-week placebo-controlled period followed by a dose-blind long-term extension
design.quote: we report the results of TANGO ( NCT03352557 ), a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group and multiple-dose long-term trial of gosuranemab—a monoclonal antibody to N-terminal tau

phase.quote: The authors present the results of a phase 2 study of gosuranemab, a monoclonal antibody targeting N-terminal tau, in patients with early Alzheimer’s disease.

n.quote: A total of 654 participants were randomized (updated from the preplanned 528 participants due to overenrollment caused by fast recruitment) to one of four groups (650 participants were dosed)

n_description.value: 654 randomized; 650 dosed and included in the full analysis set (four participants were randomized but not dosed and were excluded from the analysis)
n_description.quote: Efficacy analyses were performed on the full analysis set (that is, all randomized participants who received the study treatment (gosuranemab or placebo)). Four participants were randomized but not dosed and excluded from the analysis.

population.value: Adults aged 50–80 years with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) due to AD or mild AD dementia by NIA-AA criteria, with a CDR global score of 0.5 (MCI) or 0.5–1.0 (mild AD dementia), MMSE 22–30, and evidence of amyloid pathology
population.quote: The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the safety and tolerability of gosuranemab in patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) due to AD and those with mild AD dementia.
population.location: Main, final paragraph; eligibility detail in Methods, 'Eligibility criteria'

followup.value: 78-week double-blind, placebo-controlled period, followed by a dose-blind long-term extension analysed up to week 104
followup.quote: This randomized, parallel-group study consisted of a 78-week double-blind, placebo-controlled phase and a subsequent dose-blind LTE phase.

intervention.value: Intravenous gosuranemab for 78 weeks: low-dose (125 mg q4w, n = 58; 375 mg q12w, n = 58), intermediate-dose (600 mg q4w, n = 106) or high-dose (2,000 mg q4w, n = 214), versus placebo (q4w, n = 214)
intervention.quote: low-dose (125 mg once every 4 weeks (q4w), n = 58; 375 mg q12w, n = 58), intermediate-dose (600 mg q4w, n = 106) or high-dose (2,000 mg q4w, n = 214) gosuranemab

comparator.quote: (2) intermediate-dose gosuranemab (600 mg q4w), (3) high-dose gosuranemab (2,000 mg q4w) or (4) placebo (0.9% NaCl q4w)

biomarker_confirmation.value: Evidence of amyloid pathology confirmed by amyloid PET (visual read) or CSF testing
biomarker_confirmation.quote: Participants must also have demonstrated evidence of amyloid pathology, confirmed by amyloid PET (visual read) or CSF testing.

outcomes.name: Incidence of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) during the placebo-controlled period
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: For the placebo-controlled period of this study, the primary endpoint was the incidence of AEs and SAEs.
outcomes.effect_estimate: Any AE: placebo 181/214 (84.6%) vs total gosuranemab 381/436 (87.4%); SAEs: placebo 26/214 (12.1%) vs total gosuranemab 50/436 (11.5%)
outcomes.quote: Overall, the incidence of adverse events (AEs) and serious AEs (SAEs) was similar across the treatment and placebo groups.
outcomes.location: Results, 'Primary endpoint results for gosuranemab safety and tolerability'

outcomes.name: Change in the Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) score from baseline over time at week 78
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: The secondary endpoints were (1) the change in the CDR-SB score from baseline over time at week 78, and (2) the incidence of anti-gosuranemab serum antibody responses over time up to week 90.
outcomes.effect_estimate: Difference from placebo at week 78: –0.01 (high dose), 0.38 (intermediate dose), 0.34 (low dose); adjusted mean change from baseline: placebo 1.85, low dose 2.20, intermediate dose 2.24, high dose 1.85
outcomes.confidence_interval: Adjusted mean change from baseline at week 78: 1.85 (95% CI 1.48, 2.21) high dose; 2.24 (95% CI 1.75, 2.72) intermediate dose; 2.20 (95% CI 1.72, 2.67) low dose; 1.85 (95% CI 1.48, 2.22) placebo
outcomes.p_value: P = 0.9778 (high dose); P = 0.1965 (intermediate dose); P = 0.2362 (low dose)
outcomes.quote: The difference between the treated groups and the placebo group at week 78 was –0.01 ( P = 0.9778) for the high-dose group, 0.38 ( P = 0.1965) for the intermediate-dose group

outcomes.name: Incidence of anti-gosuranemab serum antibody responses over time up to week 90 (immunogenicity)

outcomes.quote: The incidence of treatment-emergent anti-gosuranemab antibody responses was low at all time points and similar between all gosuranemab dose groups and the placebo group.

limitations: Biological/technical limitation: targeting an N-terminal tau epitope may not sufficiently capture the extracellular tau species responsible for mediating tau pathology propagation
Pathological tau species may spread through pathways not accessible to monoclonal antibodies, such as exosomes or nanotubes, and most tau resides inside neurons
Preclinical tau transgenic mouse models are unsuitable for testing therapeutics aimed at intercepting extracellular tau, calling into question their predictive value
The study was affected by the COVID-19 pandemic; visit-scheduling flexibility kept discontinuation low at the expense of increased protocol deviations
Limited data were collected during the LTE period due to the early termination of the study
Improved fluid measures are needed to understand the extracellular availability of pathological tau

risk_of_bias.judgement: The trial was sponsored and funded by Biogen, the statistical analysis was performed by Biogen statisticians/programmers, and most authors are current or former Biogen employees and shareholders.

risk_of_bias.judgement: No adjustment for multiple comparisons was made across the many secondary and exploratory comparisons reported, so nominal P values (including the significant ADAS-Cog13, p-tau181, total tau and lateral ventricle results) are unadjusted.
risk_of_bias.quote: Analyses were two-sided at a 5% significance level. No adjustments were made for multiple comparisons.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The long-term extension was terminated early for lack of efficacy and no participant completed it, so LTE analyses rest on truncated follow-up.
risk_of_bias.quote: The LTE period of the study was terminated early owing to the lack of efficacy demonstrated upon readout after the placebo-controlled period.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Pandemic-driven scheduling flexibility increased protocol deviations, which the document states were generally balanced across groups.
risk_of_bias.quote: This flexibility made possible the low discontinuation rate observed in the study, at the expense of increased protocol deviations.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The delayed-start / LTE comparisons are labelled post hoc by the document itself and are limited by early termination.
risk_of_bias.quote: Data from the LTE period were analyzed up to week 104, during which the sample size was still substantial (the n for each group was >50% of the total sample size at baseline).

risk_of_bias.judgement: Enrollment exceeded the preplanned 528 participants, reaching 654 because of fast recruitment.
risk_of_bias.quote: A total of 654 participants were randomized (updated from the preplanned 528 participants due to overenrollment caused by fast recruitment)

disagreements.question: Does target engagement of extracellular N-terminal tau translate into reduced tau pathology or clinical benefit?
disagreements.position: This document concludes that gosuranemab bound extracellular N-terminal tau robustly but that this engagement produced neither a reduction in tau PET-measured pathology nor clinical benefit.
disagreements.quote: Thus, gosuranemab effectively bound extracellular N-terminal tau, but this binding did not reduce the accumulation of pathological tau as detected by tau PET.

disagreements.question: Are tau transgenic mouse models predictive of clinical efficacy for anti-tau antibodies?
disagreements.position: This document argues the predictive value of these preclinical models is questionable, since agents effective in mice have failed clinically.
disagreements.quote: However, similar to gosuranemab, these agents have failed to demonstrate a clear clinical benefit in patients with early AD, calling into question the predictive value of these mouse studies for clinical efficacy.

disagreements.question: Is the N-terminus of tau the right therapeutic epitope?
disagreements.position: This document argues an N-terminal epitope may not capture the extracellular tau species that propagate pathology, and that intracellular tau may be the more important target.
disagreements.quote: Thus, targeting an N-terminal tau epitope may not sufficiently capture extracellular tau species responsible for mediating tau pathology propagation.

disagreements.question: Have all anti-tau antibody trials in AD been negative?
disagreements.position: This document notes that, in contrast to the negative early-AD trials, semorinemab showed partial efficacy on one coprimary endpoint in moderate AD in the Lauriet trial.
disagreements.attributed_to: The TANGO investigators, citing the Lauriet trial of semorinemab
disagreements.quote: By contrast, in the Lauriet trial, semorinemab demonstrated partial efficacy compared to placebo, with a reduced rate of cognitive decline based on one coprimary endpoint (ADAS-Cog11 scores) in participants with moderate AD .
